newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat hits 2-1/2 month low on rain, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat hits 2-1/2 month low on rain, exports.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on rain over the weekend in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region, traders said.
"In wheat, it was weather plus disappointing exports for wheat and we're not that far away from new crop harvest," said Joe Victor, analyst for Allendale Inc.
New crop July touched a session low of $3.63 per bushel, a 2-1/2 month low and the lowest level for that contract since $3.61 was touched on March 11.
Beneficial moisture fell in northwest Kansas and portions of Colorado and Nebraska.

Weather Services Corp said the central and southern Plains received 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain with some locally heavier amounts. WSC also noted the chance of a few light showers Monday through Thursday.
Pressure also came from Tuesday's USDA weekly export inspections report, traders said.
USDA said for the week ended May 22, U.S. wheat inspected for export totalled 6.960 million bushels, below expectations for 10 million to 14 million bushels.
Wheat closed three to 14-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 11-1/2 at $3.63-1/2 a bushel.

Fund selling totaled between 17.0 million and 20.0 million bushels, led by Prudential Securities sale of 7.5 million bushels of July, traders said. LIT America sold 5.5 million bushels of July and E.D. and F. Man sold three million bushels of July, traders said.
Commercials were the key buyers with Cargill Inc purchasing up to 4.5 million bushels of July and FIMAT Futures buying five million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 25,000 contracts, above the 17,069 traded Friday.
Spread dealings centered on Tenco Inc's spread of 400,000 bushels of September/July at 7-3/4 to eight cents, premium September, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, below the 11,358 traded Friday.
